_about: The house guide's database: documents in collections, like the claude.ai artifact database the book was first built on. server/server.py stores them in SQLite and enforces these rules. Paths: 'collection/doc' (even number of segments = a document). In a family page every home except the first keeps its collections under '<home id>-' (e.g. 'hamra-private'); the rules apply to the name without that prefix.

levels.view: anyone who may open the guide (signed out too when PUBLIC=1)

wiki.about: Public articles, plus three special documents. Everything here may be seen by guests and buyers – never wifi passwords, key locations, alarm codes or money.

<article id>.title: string
<article id>.cat: Overview | Rooms | How it works | Your stay | Garden & pool | Roof terrace | Facades & exterior | Materials & finishes | Dimensions & data | Drawings & documents | …
<article id>.room: '<floor index>:<room name>' – ties the article to a room in the 3D model (e.g. '0:Kitchen')
<article id>.body: string – Markdown-light: blank lines, '## ' headings, '- ' lists

rows.group: Emergency | Service | Tradespeople | Purchase & building | Other

rows.kind: Built | Bought | Installed | Renovated | Repaired | Serviced | …

wiki.i18n_rule: i18n.<lang>.facts and i18n.<lang>.captions are aligned by index with the English facts/images: keep the lengths equal.

private.about: Owner only. Articles (same shape as wiki, e.g. p-* notes, stay-access with codes) plus these table documents, each { rows: [...] }.

docs.contacts: same rows as wiki/contacts – ALL of them; the public ones are copied to wiki/contacts on save
docs.timeline: same rows as wiki/timeline plus cost; the public ones are copied to wiki/timeline on save

rental.kind: Holiday lets | Seasonal lets | Long-term let

leads.about: Viewing requests from buyers (only when the guide is for sale, house.json buyer: true). Each visitor writes only leads/<their own id>.
